author: Iron
body:
Hey guys!

Recently I saw some of the rule changes that were made and decided that we should discuss them. Before I state these changes. I would like to say this is a discussion. I hope this doesn't turn into salt, please lets try and keep it civil. To begin, "Preventing someone from obtaining a kill (such as shooting yourself when falling into the void) will also not be tolerated."  I just noticed this one actually. However, I am personally baffled by it. As far as I am aware, I have been informed that this is not possible (Shooting yourself when falling into the void). Moreover, if this is the case I am quite curious as what led to this conversation. I am directly quoting ALM here: "there is literally a line in the tracker code that says shooting yourself doesn't count." With this being said I would like to hear your views on these few rules! :)

Thanks!
Let the non-salty discussion commence.


EDIT: I also personally jump into the void to run away quite a lot. So I think its a bit weird if we punish for this.

replies.author: hasl
replies.body:
Here are the new revisions:

>>> ADDITIONS <<<
  • A9 - Threatening someone in any way, on most Avicus services, will not be tolerated. This may include, but is not limited to, DDOS, Dox, and death threats of any form. Their are exceptions to this rule on Avicus Teamspeak, depending on the channel you are in.
  • C3 - The mods listed below are strictly not allowed to use:
    1. Sorting inventory mods
    2. Fly mods
    3. Aimbots
    4. Toggle-crouch mods that allow crouching while using a Minecraft interface (inventories, menus, chat)
    5. Minimaps that reveals the positions of creatures, players or underground caves/tunnels
    6. Auto-swing mods
    7. Mods that assist in switching tools
    8. X-ray mods or texture packs
    9. Mods that enhance player visibility (enlarged name tags)
    10. Mods that enhance sprinting capabilities
    11. Mods that allow you to see enemy health
    12. Macros, autoclickers, multiple attack buttons, editing hardware or having software to allow clicking than humanly possible, changing default mouse interactions, etc. The general rule as to how you should click is one button, one finger, one click.
  • C5 - Do not intentionally make it look as though you are using a hack client. Doing so will result in a punishment.

>>> EDITATIONS <<<

  • B1 - Your Minecraft username and skin must be appropriate for all ages. Objectionable skins will not be tolerated. Objectionable usernames and any username that gives the impression of or slightly relates to something objectionable will result in punishment.
  • B8 - Combat logging (logging off or leaving your team in anticipation of dying) is strictly not permitted.
  • E1 - All server rules apply with the exception of spawn-blocking, spawn-killing, team griefing, combat logging and team spleefing.

replies.author: hasl
replies.body:
Remember when Porky posted that thread saying "Do not intentionally act like you are using hacks, you will be punished." and it was a 20 page flamewar. A complete warzone. Made history.

Sound familiar? 

Despite knowing what the community's reaction may be, you still proceeded to make the change, without our input, even though we're are the ones affected, mostly.

I understand rule F2 "There is a one week grace period for rule changes" should stop confusions, but I believe consulting the community about this for feedback would've been better; this way you don't go back on yourself when you make a mistake.
